title: Residue and Coprimality Structure of Sylvester's Sequence

problemStatement.formal: a_0=2,\ a_{n+1}=a_n^2-a_n+1:\ \text{prove } a_{n+1}-1=\prod_{k\le n} a_k,\ \gcd(a_i,a_j)=1\ (i\ne j),\ a_n \text{ odd } (n\ge1),\ a_n\equiv 1 \pmod 6\ (n\ge2).
problemStatement.plain: Sylvester's sequence $2,3,7,43,1807,\dots$ has each term one more than the product of all earlier terms. That forces a rigid arithmetic skeleton: every term past the first is odd, every term is $\equiv 1$ modulo each earlier term (so the terms are pairwise coprime), and from $7$ on every term is $\equiv 1 \pmod 6$. Formalize this structure.

syl_odd (:118): every term past the first is odd
insights: The entire arithmetic skeleton (Euclid product, residue mod earlier terms, coprimality, parity, mod-6) descends from ONE factorization: a_{n+1}-1 = aₙ(aₙ-1).
mod-6 needs no case analysis: 6 ∣ aₙ-1 self-propagates because aₙ-1 is a factor of a_{n+1}-1 = aₙ(aₙ-1); Nat.le_induction from a₂=7 closes it.
Oddness (n≥1) is structural: aₙ(aₙ-1) is a product of consecutive integers hence even, so a_{n+1}=even+1 is odd.
ℕ truncated subtraction in the recurrence is defused once by substituting aₙ = p+2; ring/omega then close every arithmetic identity without ℤ-lifting.
